title: STILL PRESENT (r3): the wrong-person leg's taken-over stand-down is read-time only — apply_wrong_person still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status; the guarded mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person SQL is never wired in

evidence: reference_checks_api.gleam:38 `use id <- decode.optional_field("reference_call_id", None, decode.optional(decode.string))` — client.gleam:3555 `Ok(_) -> {` (the Result(String) payload is never read; the refetch is a whole-detail refetch: :3567 `refetch_refcheck_effect(model)`).

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): N14 — Escape-to-close stays on the menu div, which never receives focus after clicking the ⋯ button
evidence: :745 `// r2 (N14): Escape closes the menu (the confirm_modal pattern).` :747 `event.on("keydown", menu_escape_decoder(msg.UserToggledRefcheckMenu(` — the listener is on the absolutely-positioned menu div (a SIBLING of the ⋯ button, :719 `html.div([class("relative flex-shrink-0 self-start")], [`), which contains the button). No autofocus/tabindex moves focus into the menu on open.
detail: After clicking ⋯, focus stays on the button; keydown events bubble through the button's ancestors (not the sibling menu div), so click-then-Escape does nothing. Handler fires only if the user first clicks a menu item.
recommended_fix: Attach the keydown handler to the ⋯ button (or autofocus the menu div on open) so the natural click-then-Escape flow closes the menu.

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): N5 — the edit-open path still unconditionally overwrites another row's in-progress typed trio (only the success-clear half was scoped)
